summary: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task?
takeaways: Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task?
We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment.

Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units.
